description.summary: Tiny utilities for small and embedded systems
description.p: BusyBox combines tiny versions of many common UNIX utilities into a single small executable. It provides minimalist replacements for the most common utilities you would usually find on your desktop system (i.e., ls, cp, mv, mount, tar, etc.). The utilities in BusyBox generally have fewer options than their full-featured GNU cousins; however, the options that are included provide the expected functionality and behave very much like their GNU counterparts.

This package installs the BusyBox binary. The links for its utilities are not part of the package: a trigger creates them whenever programs are installed or removed, for every utility that no other installed package provides.

trigger.script:
if [ "$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX" = "/tools" ]; then BUSYBOX="/tools/bin/busybox" LINK_DIRS="/tools/bin /tools/sbin" else BUSYBOX="/bin/busybox" LINK_DIRS="/usr/bin /usr/sbin" fi
# The script is run by the shell of busybox, not by /bin/sh, and it calls # the programs through busybox itself: when it runs for the first time, # there are no links yet.
# Remove the links of applets that this version no longer has. APPLETS="$("$BUSYBOX" --list)"
for DIR in $LINK_DIRS; do for LINK in "$DIR"/*; do if [ ! -L "$LINK" ]; then continue fi if [ "$("$BUSYBOX" readlink "$LINK")" != "$BUSYBOX" ]; then continue fi
case " $APPLETS " in *" ${LINK##*/} "*) ;; *) "$BUSYBOX" rm -f "$LINK" ;; esac done done
# Create the links that are missing. A name that is taken, by the program # of another package for example, is left alone. if [ "$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX" = "/tools" ]; then "$BUSYBOX" --install -s /tools/bin else # The applets that need root get their links from the busybox-suid # package, if it is installed. It reports the names that are taken as # failures. if [ -x /bin/bbsuid ]; then /bin/bbsuid --install || true fi
"$BUSYBOX" --install -s fi

maintainer-scripts.prerm:
if [ "$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX" = "/tools" ]; then BUSYBOX="/tools/bin/busybox" LINK_DIRS="/tools/bin /tools/sbin" else BUSYBOX="/bin/busybox" LINK_DIRS="/usr/bin /usr/sbin" fi
# The links belong to no package, take them away with busybox. This is run # by the shell of busybox: the link /bin/sh may be gone already. if [ "$1" = "remove" ]; then for DIR in $LINK_DIRS; do for LINK in "$DIR"/*; do if [ ! -L "$LINK" ]; then continue fi if [ "$("$BUSYBOX" readlink "$LINK")" = "$BUSYBOX" ]; then "$BUSYBOX" rm -f "$LINK" fi done done fi
